footer.about: Dan Dan The Window Man is an owner-run exterior remodeling company on West Kellogg Drive in Wichita. We replace windows and doors, install vinyl siding and gutters, and handle hail damage claims.
why: Owner Rick Timsah works with you himself
Free estimates on windows, doors and siding
Your customers say it plainly: Rick is "straightforward" with "zero upselling or pressure," the installers "left the job site clean," and the price is fair. You hold a 4.7 on 44 Google reviews.
Your site shows none of it. On a phone your number sits past the edge of the screen, the top of the homepage splits between windows and hail roofing, and Rick is never named.
So we rebuilt it around an owner who answers straight and a crew that leaves the house clean.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Exterior Company People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page of the demo: what costs you calls, and the fix.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn what you do and where.
problems: On a phone the page is twice as wide as the screen. Your number and half your menu sit past the edge, so callers scroll sideways to find you.
The top of the page is three headlines: windows, hail roofing claims, and Wichita. Google can't tell whether you're a window company or a roofer.
"Here's what our customers are saying..." has nothing under it and Rick is never named, so visitors miss the praise that wins you jobs.
fixes: Your number one tap away, with the whole menu on screen.
A headline that says exterior remodeling company in Wichita, KS.
Rick named as owner, with a real review beside each point.
cards.alsoAdd: Every page set up behind the scenes so Google and AI tools like ChatGPT know exactly what you do, where you work, and what your customers say.

cards.title: Window Replacement
cards.why: Windows are about three quarters of your written reviews, yet their page is short.
problems: The Windows page is two paragraphs, a feature list and two PDF buttons: no review, nothing on install day, and little for Google to rank.
fixes: A full page for window replacement in Wichita, KS.
Styles, glass, install steps and payment, each beside a real review.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Doors & Siding
cards.why: Door jobs come up in six of your reviews, and your site gives doors and siding a few lines.
problems: The Doors page is two short paragraphs with no reviews.
The Siding page lists eight product names with nothing under any of them, so a visitor can't tell what they'd get.
fixes: One full page for doors and siding in Wichita, with reviews from door, siding and gutter jobs.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn't think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where interest turns into a call.
problems: Your site says 10 to 5 and your Birdeye profile says 8 to 5, so a customer can't tell when to call.
Your contact page promises a reply in 24 to 48 hours, and your siding page says you return calls on weekends.
fixes: Both numbers one tap, each labeled.
One set of hours and promises, once you confirm them.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already make the case. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame, and we'll walk through this demo with you and confirm every service you offer.

onboardingQuestions: How does Rick Timsah want to be introduced on the site (owner, general manager), and who is the "Dan" in the company name? No person named Dan is confirmed, so the site never mentions one.
Real business hours: the current site says Monday to Friday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Birdeye says 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Hours are left off the demo until confirmed.
Which email address should customers use? The current site shows contact@ddtrm.com. It is not in our verified facts, so the demo shows no email.

What does the warranty cover and for how long? The old site says an exclusive lifetime warranty and a 3-year glass breakage warranty; Rick's reply to one review says his warranty covers the installation. The demo says only that the warranty covers the installation.

Which window brand does Rick install today? The old site links a ProVia warranty PDF and lists Pro-Via and Quaker windows, but ProVia's dealer locator did not list the company, so no brand is named. Are the windows still custom-built and American-made?

Licenses and certifications to verify, with numbers: Kansas lead-based renovator (KDHE), Class B building contractor, Kansas licensed roofer, and Owens Corning. Is the company insured? None of it appears on the demo.
Years in business: the earliest Google review is 2018 and Rick's reply to a 2025 review says over 12 years. What founding year can we use?

Full list of services to confirm: gutters, basement and picture windows, roofing and hail claims, metal buildings, Smart Lap and concrete siding, aluminum window and door wraps, garage doors, storm doors, window repair.
Do they want roofing and hail damage claims on the new site, and should the (833) 972-ROOF number show? The demo shows it as the roofing line on the homepage, doors and siding page and contact page.
Service area: which towns beyond Wichita should be named? The old site says only the Wichita metro area. Hillsboro appears in one review.
Electronic payments: one reviewer asked for them. The old site lists checks, Amex, Discover, MasterCard and Visa. Can they take payment by link or online?
Do they want to keep the Synchrony Bank financing offer (no monthly interest if paid in full within 18 months) exactly as worded?
Showroom: is it open to walk-ins during business hours, or by appointment?
Legal business name, logo file and brand colors. Who controls the dandanthewindowman.com domain (the site is a Hibu build)?
